newsitem.title: USA: Some Great Lakes lighthouses may change hands.
newsitem.headline: Some Great Lakes lighthouses may change hands.

text.p: The U.S. Coast Guard said Monday it has identified 17 lighthouses on the Great Lakes that are excess property and may be transferred to other government agencies or, as a last resort, sold to the public.
"In a time of downsizing and trying to make tax dollars stretch we have to look at this," a spokesman at the Coast Guard's Great Lakes headquarters in Cleveland said.

The 17 properties are considered too expensive to maintain and excess to government needs, the spokesman said. The General Services Administration could turn them over to other government agencies or to state or city governments.

If the properties are still not claimed they could be auctioned to the public. The Coast Guard would continue to maintain the lights themselves even after the buildings changed hands, the spokesman said.
The Coast Guard currently operates 144 lighthouses on the Great Lakes.
